merger_description:
Foresight Kinetic CV UK HoldCo Limited (the **Buyer**) will:

* acquire Infrastructure Capital Services Pty Limited as trustee for the ICG Kinetic Trust’s (the **Seller**’s) entire shareholding (of approximately 24.4%) in Kinetic UK Holdco, Limited (the **Target**), and
* as the Seller’s nominee, subscribe for additional shares to restore the Seller’s proportionate holding to around 29.9% following an earlier equity subscription by TPG Lux 2025 SC XI, S.à r.l. (**TPG**)

(the **Acquisition**).

The Buyer is an investment holding vehicle for Foresight Kinetic CV SCSp's (**CV**’s) investment in the Target. CV is a Luxembourg special limited partnership established as a continuation fund.

Foresight Group Holdings Limited (**Foresight Group**) is a London Stock Exchange-listed investment manager. It invests in renewable energy, battery storage, grid infrastructure, natural capital, and social, transport and digital infrastructure. The Seller and Buyer are and will remain ultimately controlled by Foresight Group.

The Target is the holding company of the Kinetic group and the Go-Ahead Group, which provide bus and rail passenger transport services in Australia, New Zealand, the UK, Ireland, Norway, Sweden and Singapore. Its rail operations are conducted outside Australia through Go-Ahead. The Target is incorporated in England and Wales.

TPG currently holds approximately 75.5% of the shares in the Target and controls the Target. Post-Acquisition, TPG will hold approximately 70.1% of the shares in the Target and will continue to control the Target.

Foresight Group will retain exclusive management and control of CV through Foresight Kinetic GP S.à r.l.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. aside from their existing interest in the Target, there are no
horizontal overlaps or vertical relationships between the
Foresight Group and the Target
b. the increment to their existing interest in the Target is small
c. the Acquisition will not result in any substantive change in
the control or day-to-day operation of the Target, which
remains under the control of TPG.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
The ACCC also considered the potential application of section
51ABD of the Act. However, the applicant submitted that it was
uncertain whether that provision applied. Having regard to the
particular circumstances, including the consequences of non-
notification in reliance on section 51ABD if it was found not to apply,
the ACCC considered it appropriate to make a determination on the
basis that the acquisition provisions in the Act apply to the
Acquisition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
